problem.text: HumanEval exposed only temperature and top-p and lacked ChatML and DeepSeek prompt presets.

reasoning.text: The merge integrates PR #32 by replacing TopPSampler with the existing ComboSampler and adding two opt-in prompt formats, rather than implementing evaluation-specific sampling filters.

impact.text: New CLI controls expose min-p, top-k, repetition penalties and temperature-last. Defaults retain temperature 0.6 and top-p 0.6, with the additional filters neutral or disabled.

source_notes.text: The supplied merge comparison establishes that the tree is identical to second parent 3c9ede55404c8ecce54494657f23f7056ea36a1a: these are first-parent integration changes, not additional merge-only content.
PR #32 is attributed to gakada; its available body is empty and supplies no further rationale or benchmark evidence.
The second-parent annotation already records the top-k argument-type concern.

limitations: No model generation, PyTorch indexing, CUDA sampling or HumanEval scoring was executed; prompt compatibility and benchmark effects remain unmeasured.
The bounded execution checks argparse and Python list slicing, not the repository sampler.

claims.text: Both new presets repeat the problem in the request and an assistant-prefilled Python fence. ChatML supplies system/user/assistant delimiters; DeepSeek uses its User and Assistant markers. Existing encoding requests special-token recognition and BOS, and output reconstruction retains a four-space completion prefix.

ComboSampler places penalties before temperature, min-p, top-k, top-p and categorical sampling. temp_last moves temperature after the filters; temperature zero instead selects argmax after penalties and bypasses filtering. CustomSampler substitutes no-ops and inserts sorting or normalization prerequisites.

Min-p uses the largest probability times min_p as its cutoff; zero disables it. Top-k masks sorted positions starting at k and is disabled below one. Repetition penalty 1.0 is neutral. Thus temperature-last changes which distribution supplies probability-based filtering thresholds.
The same sampler is passed to each job. Completion termination, JSONL writing and optional functional-correctness evaluation are unchanged by this merge.

findings.description: The integrated CLI retains the second parent's float-valued top-k mismatch.
findings.trigger: Run HumanEval with --top_k 5 and nonzero temperature, reaching sampling.
findings.actual_behavior: The parser produces 5.0, which passes the enabled-filter check and reaches SS_TopK.run unchanged as a tensor slice boundary, expected to raise TypeError. Default 0.0 disables this step; temperature zero bypasses it.

verification.description: Traced the script entry through main and ComboSampler. Whole-parent-tree SS_TopK construction search found TopKSampler, ComboSampler and an integer-valued test construction. The affected reach is the new HumanEval CLI path, not all sampler users.
A standard-library reproduction parsed 5 as 5.0 and observed TypeError when slicing a list; the default remained disabled.
verification.limits: List slicing models the type mismatch but does not execute PyTorch or GPU sampling.

annotation.summary: Integrates ChatML and DeepSeek HumanEval prompts and ComboSampler controls, retaining a suspected enabled-top-k CLI type mismatch.
